office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital, and transportation budgets, serving a two-year term.
race_blurb: Thirteen-year Democratic incumbent Mia Su-Ling Gregerson, vice-chair of House Appropriations, faces first-time Republican candidate Yuri Marinchik, who took the second primary slot by 600 votes.

candidates.summary: State Representative since 2013, former SeaTac mayor and Appropriations vice-chair, running on state programs she helped deliver such as free school meals and right to repair.
highlights: Cites free school meals for every student, emergency food aid and free transit for kids [S1]
Sponsored the 2025 Right to Repair Act for consumer electronics [S11]
Voted for ESSB 6346 (2026 income tax over $1 million), ESHB 1296 and rent stabilization [S3][S4][S5]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million; no campaign statements on taxes found.

spending.basis: Runs entirely on expanded state programs: universal free school meals, emergency food aid and free youth transit.

housing.basis: Voted for rent stabilization in 2025; no campaign housing statement found.

experience.basis: In the House since 2013, Appropriations vice-chair, former SeaTac mayor, with enacted bills.

tech.basis: Sponsored the Right to Repair Act, which requires electronics makers to provide parts and tools and restricts parts pairing.

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates; no statement of her own on reproductive or LGBTQ+ policy.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, the 2025 amendments to the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: First-time Republican candidate and small-business owner running against career politicians on lower costs, no new taxes, and public safety.
highlights: Says new taxes will not make things better and the state spends more than it earns [S2]
Calls for lower housing and energy costs and stronger public safety [S1]
Signed the U.S. Term Limits pledge on congressional term limits [S6]

taxes.basis: States new taxes will not make things better; cites car-tab and RTA tax grievances.

spending.basis: Says the state faces a shortfall and is spending more than it earns.

safety.basis: Calls for stronger public safety and cites property crime and break-ins, without stating enforcement or prevention policies.

experience.basis: No elected experience; runs explicitly against career politicians.

reform.basis: Signed a congressional term-limits pledge and frames his run against career politicians.
